generation.hypothesis: Single-phase noble-metal high-entropy-alloy nanoframework formation and crystal-structure selection will be governed by which noble metal first nucleates a lattice and catalyzes hydrogen dissociation. Pt, Ir, or Ru should seed incorporation of later-reduced transition metals, whereas subsequent thermal activation and Pt:Ru balance should determine kinetic retention of fcc structure versus conversion to thermodynamically favored Ru-rich hcp structure.
generation.material_initial_state: Near-spherical, compositionally uniform precursor particles will be prepared from homogeneously mixed aqueous (NH4)2PtCl6 and selected Co, Cu, Ni, Fe, Ru, Ir, and/or Pd salts with NH4Cl. Compositions will span quinary through octonary noble-metal/transition-metal mixtures.
generation.intervention: Uniform precursor particles will be reduced in hydrogen at about 300°C. Noble-metal identity will be varied among Pt, Ir, Ru, and Pd, with noble-metal-free NiCoCuFe as a control. In PtxNiCoCuRuy, Pt:Ru ratios will range from approximately 3:1 to 1:4, followed by optional secondary heating at 400–500°C.
generation.conditions: Primary formation will occur under H2 near 300°C, with comparison treatments near 200°C and 450°C. Phase tuning will use 400–500°C. Methanol oxidation will be evaluated in deoxygenated aqueous 0.5 M H2SO4 and 0.5 M CH3OH.
generation.structural_mediator: The mediator will be a porous, self-supported three-dimensional nanoarm framework containing a homogeneous single-phase solid solution. Pt- and Ir-seeded lattices should favor fcc structure, Ru-seeded lattices should favor hcp structure, and Pt–Ru systems should contain tunable proportions of Pt-based fcc and Ru-based hcp domains.
generation.mechanism: Pt, Ir, or Ru salts should reduce first below about 300°C and establish their characteristic lattice. Dissociative H2 adsorption on that newborn surface should generate reactive hydrogen that reduces nearby Ni, Co, Cu, and Fe, allowing their incorporation into the existing lattice. Pd should fail because hydrogen desorption is less favorable and more strongly activated. In Pt–Ru alloys, fcc structure should initially persist kinetically; heating should overcome an approximately 0.45 eV barrier and permit fcc-to-hcp conversion.
generation.predicted_outcome: PtNiCoCuRuIr should reach roughly 2600 mA/mgPt methanol-oxidation mass activity, about 15-fold above Pt black, with an electrochemically active surface area near 100 m2/gPt and higher sustained current. Greater Ru content and reheating should increase hcp fraction; Pt1Ni1Co1Cu1Ru4 should become predominantly hcp by roughly 400–500°C.
generation.baseline: Pt black will provide a catalytic baseline of about 170 mA/mgPt and 18 m2/gPt. Unreheated Pt-rich PtNiCoCuRu formed near 300°C will provide the predominantly fcc structural baseline.
generation.boundary: The mechanism should apply to Pt-, Ir-, or Ru-seeded systems under H2, but not PdNiCoCuFe or noble-metal-free NiCoCuFe. Phase tuning should apply to PtxNiCoCuRuy between Pt:Ru ratios of 3:1 and 1:4 over 300–500°C; Ru enrichment alone at 300°C may not produce predominantly hcp material.
generation.uncertainty: Composition-dependent kinetic barriers may shift the fcc-to-hcp transition temperature by roughly 50°C.

falsification_experiment.design: Compare matched Pt-, Ir-, Ru-, Pd-, and noble-metal-free compositions after H2 treatment near 300°C, and follow Pt1Ni1Co1Cu1Ru4 during heating to 500°C.
measurements: Temperature-resolved atomic-resolution imaging and diffraction of fcc/hcp structure
Methanol-oxidation mass activity, active surface area, and sustained current
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis will be falsified if Pd or noble-metal-free controls form equally homogeneous single-phase alloys at 300°C, or if Ru-rich Pt–Ru material retains fcc structure through 500°C without an increasing hcp fraction.
